newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Gehe sells drugs production unit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gehe sells drugs production unit.

text.p: Gehe AG, Germany's largest pharmaceutical wholesaler, on Tuesday said it would sell its drugs manufacturing operation in order to concentrate resources on expanding its position as a global drugs wholesaler.

In total, Gehe will earn 1.2 billion marks ($780.5 million) from the sales of four separate groups and the majority stake in a fifth unit which all produce generic drugs -- medication whose patent protection has lapsed.

The largest of the four groups, Azupharma GmbH, will go to Swiss chemicals and drugs giant Sandoz AG for 640 million marks while Gehe's French unit GNR-pharma S.A. will be bought by German chemicals group BASF AG's Knoll AG drugs unit.
Aliud Pharma GmbH & Co. KG and allphamed Arzneimittelgesellschaft mbH will also be sold, but Gehe declined to name the buyers or prices as the deals' formalities had not yet been completed.
Earlier this summer, Gehe sold a 74.9 percent stake in its eastern German Jenapharm GmbH group for 500 million marks, to Schering AG, the world's largest maker of oral contraceptives.

The step, part of a broad drugs industry consolidation, moves Gehe closer to reaching its goal of numbering among the top global companies in each of its three core business areas, renting health equipment, shipping drugs, and selling drugs wholesale.

"Our problem was we were too small in the production area to keep pace with the world's big players, so it makes sense to divest the division and concentrate on the other areas," Gehe chief financial officer Karl-Gerhard Eick told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Analysts praised Gehe management for focusing on the company's strengths but were not persuaded to alter their recommendations, now largely at hold.

Similarly, the share market first welcomed the news, sending Gehe shares to a new high at 110.50 marks. But traders later took profits, leaving shares to close bourse trade nearly one percent lower at 107.00 marks.
On the whole, Eick said he was satisfied with the group's share price saying it reflected the group's profile accurately.
Gehe's operating business was "satisfactory" and for the year the group expected to boost sales to between 20 and 21 billion marks, up from 1995's 19.2 billion turnover, Eick said.

While Gehe will feel the loss of the drugs production unit which in 1995 contributed three percent to turnover and nine percent to the group's 360 million mark pre-tax profit, Eick said strong internal growth and improve currency relationships will keep results strong.

While the sale delivers an added bonus of eliminating potential conflicts of interest between business areas, Eick said the move was not directly related to Gehe's stalled attempt to take over U.K. group Lloyds Chemists.

Gehe and U.K. group UniChem Plc have been locked in a 10-month bidding war for for Lloyds which has currently been stalled as U.K. monopoly authorities scrutinise how well each group has complied with certain requirements.

Eick said Gehe has met its requirements and now awaits an answer from the Office of Fair Trade Office. Only after receiving comments from the office will Gehe be able to decide whether it will submit another bid for the group.
"We are still interested in Lloyds Chemists," Eick said, declining however to be drawn out on how high the bid may be, and when it may be made.
